subject: Emerald connector: validation & test-harness
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@emerald.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Emerald connector: validation & test-harness

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product team here at Emerald is excited about the potential to ship a ForgeBridge connector powered by Redwood. Before we commit to the integration timeline, our engineering leadership asked for a short technical validation plan and a reference solution design we can run against our QA cadence.

High-level asks from our side:
- A one-page reference architecture showing auth, network boundaries (VPC peering / private egress), and where the model variants live.
- A test harness / acceptance matrix for the POC: E2E flows, latency checks, token accounting, and failure/fallback behaviour.
- Data handling notes (retention, masking) for compliance review.

Target timeline: start validation the week of Jun 14, wrap POC in 3 weeks. Can Redwood provide a design + test matrix we can run in our staging environment? We can provide a Jira board and test accounts.

Attachments: emerald-initial-requirements.pdf (spec), staging-api-creds-stub.txt

Best,
Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Integrations, Emerald Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@emerald.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emerald connector: validation & test-harness

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Laura and I sketched a concise plan and attached two artifacts: a Redwood reference design (PDF) and an initial POC test matrix (XLSX). Short summary below.

What we will provide (week of Jun 14 kickoff):
- Reference design: network/data flow, auth patterns (mutual TLS + token), model routing options (hosted vs. dedicated) and recommended quantization profile for cost/latency tradeoffs. Attachment: redwood-emerald-ref-design-v1.pdf
- Test harness: acceptance matrix with E2E scenarios, synthetic load profiles for latency SLO validation, KV cache hit rate checks, and regression prompts for quality monitoring. Attachment: emerald-poc-test-matrix.xlsx
- A lightweight smoke runner (python script) we can share to run in Emerald staging; it will exercise auth, token lifecycle, and a handful of canonical prompts.

Responsibilities / ask from Emerald:
- Provide staging network details (IP allowlist / VPC config) and a sandbox API key.
- A point of contact on QA to own the Jira board you mentioned; we'll link our validation tickets.

Timeline:
- Jun 14: kickoff + environment verification
- Jun 15–24: integration + smoke tests
- Jun 25–28: performance runs and acceptance signoff

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Sergio on the partner ops side and our infra engineer.

Attachments: redwood-emerald-ref-design-v1.pdf, emerald-poc-test-matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Emerald POC: scope & internal owners (internal)

Laura / Sergio — moving this to an internal thread to confirm owners and risks before the kickoff. Summary of action items and potential gotchas: 

Scope we committed: auth+network, baseline latency/perf, and a basic quality safety regression set. NOT in scope for this POC: custom model training, private on-prem deployment.

Internal owners (proposed):
- Integration + reference design: Laura Bennett (owner)
- Partner ops / onboarding: Sergio Alvarez (owner)
- Performance/infra validation: Rishi (co-owner), will coordinate with infra on kernel tuning & batching parameters.

Technical risks / mitigations:
- Network: Emerald will be routing from their VPC; we need their allowlist and confirm NAT behavior. Mitigation: provide an NGINX bastion pattern in the reference design and verify egress IPs.
- Data compliance: their asks around masking/PII retention require we document ephemeral storage and log retention. Mitigation: include explicit retention language and a sample KMS flow in the design.
- Latency variance under burst: include an automated runner to measure p50/p95/p99 under synthetic bursts; if p99 > 1.5s we recommend a dedicated routing policy during peak windows.

Deliverables before kickoff: reference design v1 + test matrix (already attached to Priya). I’ll draft the kickoff agenda and send invites for a Jun 14 11:00 AM PT slot unless I hear otherwise.

Rishi
